name: Zoho CRM
oneLiner: Per-user CRM billed flat across five editions (Free through Ultimate); every paid edition costs 20-34% less per seat when billed annually instead of month-to-month.
summary: Zoho CRM prices Free, Standard, Professional, Enterprise and Ultimate purely per user, with no contact-count tiers to budget around. Each paid edition raises automation, AI and customization limits, and costs 20 to 34 percent less per seat when billed annually instead of month-to-month. Mass/marketing email sending is capped per organization per day rather than per user, and Zoho does not list a native SMS feature on its pricing or feature-comparison pages.
notFor: Teams that need native SMS/texting billed through the CRM itself (not a listed feature on any edition; would need a separate integration)
Organizations sending more than about 60,000 mass marketing emails a month (even Ultimate caps org-wide mass email at 2,000/day)
Buyers who want the annual per-seat price without prepaying the year (month-to-month costs 20-34% more per seat)
pros: Free plan for up to 3 users with workflow automation, APIs and mobile apps, no credit card required
15-day free trial on every paid edition, no credit card required
Flat per-user pricing across all 5 editions, with no contact-count tiers to budget around
No long-term contract: pay-as-you-go monthly or yearly, and switch plans anytime
Cheaper Lite User seats (US$12-15/month) on Enterprise and Ultimate for team members who only need limited access
cons: Month-to-month billing costs 20-34% more per seat than paying annually, on every paid edition
Mass/marketing email is capped per organization per day (250 on Standard up to 2,000 on Ultimate), not scaled per user
No native SMS/texting feature found on Zoho's own pricing or feature-comparison pages
Free plan can't send mass emails at all and is capped at 5,000 records (10MB) of storage
Extra file storage (US$4.60/5GB) and extra data storage (US$4/100MB) are recurring add-on charges, not one-time purchases
